listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Tuesday, October 13. The lead story: a drone attack hit two merchant ships off Bulgaria. One ship sank. Bulgaria's prime minister says he suspects Russia was behind the attacks, and he has summoned the Russian ambassador. In other news, President Trump's diesel deal with Russia has angered European countries. Ukraine's president has questioned Washington's motives. Voters in the United States are heading toward the midterm elections, and the BBC has a look at the key races and issues. French investigators used DNA and vehicle tracking to recover two stolen Renoir paintings. In India, authorities have removed more than 130 million names from the voter rolls, and a crackdown on protesters has followed. In technology, Python 3.15 is now released. A new open source tool lets Mac users search their files by content on their own device. In politics, Montana voters will consider a ballot measure about corporate spending. In sports, Brendan Allen won a UFC main event by fifth-round submission. San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw has been suspended one game without pay. In Atlanta, a naturalist is opposing plans to double daily visitors on Cumberland Island. The public comment deadline is October 16. Brookhaven residents have asked the city council to delay a fire station agreement. In architecture, Matterport now imports point cloud files. IES Sync for Revit has launched. In science, a study says heat slows photosynthesis in coast redwoods. Antarctic sea ice has reached its 2026 maximum, the third lowest on record. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Ship sinks in new drone attack off Bulgaria, PM summons Russian ambassador
lead.note: Bulgaria's prime minister says two merchant ships were hit by drones off the Bulgarian coast. One ship sank in the attack. He suspects Russia was behind the strikes and has summoned the Russian ambassador to explain. The item calls it a new drone attack, pointing to a continuing pattern of incidents in the region. The summary does not say who was aboard the ships or what damage was done beyond the sinking. For a reader following world news, this is a direct escalation involving a NATO and European Union member state. It adds to the wider strain between Europe and Moscow that runs through today's other coverage, including the diesel deal between Washington and Moscow.
